title: Citrine Ventures - Privacy & Deployment Security Review
summary: Introductory security posture review focusing on hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment options. Main concerns: KMS integration, SSO/SAML, RBAC scoping, audit log retention and ability to do forensics, and data residency/retention policies. Agreed to run a short pilot on Dedicated with a scoped SSO + KMS test and to share SOC2/ISO documentation.
next_steps: Redwood to send SOC2 and ISO summaries + security whitepaper (Liam)
SE to share a short dedicated pilot runbook and estimated pricing (Sofia)
Customer to validate IdP SAML metadata and share test account (Priya)
Schedule a 1-hour pilot planning call next week (Marco to propose times)

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-06-24
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 41 minutes
Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE), Sofia Alvarez (Redwood SE), Evan Brooks (Redwood SE), Anita Rao (Head of Data, Citrine), Jordan Wells (CTO), Priya Menon (Security Engineer), Marco Lin (DevOps)
---
Auto-summary (optional, autogenerated): Quick intake on security needs. Customer leans toward Dedicated but wants clear KMS/SSO story and audit log retention that fits VC compliance.
---
[00:00] Liam Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll do a quick intros and then jump into your security questions. Um, let's start with roles — can you say who you are and what you're focused on?
[00:10] Anita Rao: Hi I'm Anita, head of data at Citrine, I'm primarily worried about data classification and retention, we have a bunch of PII we need to keep control of.
[00:18] Jordan Wells: Jordan here, CTO, interested in deployment path and cost tradeoffs — we need predictable latency for some inference flows.
[00:25] Priya Menon: Priya, security engineer, I'll be driving SSO/KMS/retention acceptance criteria.
[00:30] Marco Lin: Marco, platform/devops, I'll own infra under the pilot.
[00:35] Liam Chen: Great. On Redwood side I've got Sofia and Evan who will cover the technical bits, and I'll run the procurement framing.
[00:42] Sofia Alvarez: Hey all. Quick agenda: 1) KMS/encryption story 2) SSO/SAML and RBAC 3) audit logs and retention 4) deployment options: hosted vs dedicated vs private 5) next steps. Sound good?
[00:50] Anita Rao: Yep, go ahead.
[00:52] [00:52] Evan Brooks: Just flagging we'll have a short deck after the call, but we can also drop links to the SOC2 docs.
[01:02] [01:02] Priya Menon: Awesome. Let's start with KMS — what are our options if we want customer-managed keys? Is that available on Hosted?
[01:10] Sofia Alvarez: Short answer: yes for Dedicated and Private; for Hosted we offer an option via bring-your-own-KMS for enterprise tiers — it's not the default on the public hosted endpoints today. There's a hosted KMS integration path but it depends on contract and region.
[01:26] Priya Menon: Hmm ok, so for our compliance we prefer customer-managed keys in an HSM or KMS where we control key rotation. How does Redwood handle enveloping, rotation, and key access policies?
[01:38] Sofia Alvarez: We do envelope encryption. Application-level payloads are encrypted with per-request DEKs, those DEKs are wrapped with the CMK in the customer's KMS. Rotation is transparent — new CMKs are supported and we provide guidance to rewrap. Access to the CMK is gated by IAM policies on the cloud provider and we can tie that to RBAC in our Private installation.
[01:54] Marco Lin: Quick clarification — in Dedicated will the Redwood runtime be inside our VPC or is it still a managed single-tenant but outside our network?
[02:04] Liam Chen: Good question. Dedicated is single-tenant with customer-dedicated GPU pools; options exist for VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink depending on region. For full VPC-hosted deployment you usually go Private, but Dedicated can be configured with network isolation and VPC connectivity.
[02:18] Jordan Wells: So if we need full network isolation for sensitive models, Private is the path?
[02:22] Sofia Alvarez: Correct. Private gives you the customer-controlled control plane and the runtime can run in your VPC or on-prem. Dedicated is a middle ground — predictable capacity and data isolation but less control over the private network unless you select the VPC peering add-on.
[02:36] [02:36] Priya Menon: Ok on SSO: we run Okta and Azure AD. We need SAML 2.0 and SCIM for user provisioning. Can Redwood do those?
[02:45] Evan Brooks: Yes, we support SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM for provisioning in both Dedicated and Private. Hosted supports SSO, but SCIM provisioning is typically part of the enterprise package — we can enable it for you in a pilot.
[03:00] Priya Menon: How is RBAC scoped? We want role separation: devs can't access production logs and only a small security group can request key rotations.
[03:08] Sofia Alvarez: RBAC is resource-scoped: you can define roles for model routes, environments (dev/staging/prod), and KMS admin operations. For Private we integrate with your IdP group mappings; for Dedicated we also support group-based roles mapped from SAML assertions or SCIM groups.
[03:22] Marco Lin: Is there an API to revoke tokens or sessions centrally? We need the ability to kill sessions quickly in incident response.
[03:29] Evan Brooks: Yes, token revocation and session invalidation are available through our admin API. There's also an audit event we emit, and we can set short TTLs on tokens for higher security profiles.
[03:41] [03:41] Anita Rao: Audit logs — how long do you retain them and can we push logs to our SIEM? We need six months of immutable logs for forensic timelines.
[03:51] Liam Chen: Out of the box we retain 90 days for hosted logs, but for Dedicated and Private you can configure longer retention or export logs to customer-managed S3 or to SIEMs like Splunk or Datadog. For regulatory ask of six months we recommend pushing to your own storage and applying immutability controls.
[04:09] Priya Menon: Are audit logs tamper-evident? Do you sign them or provide append-only storage?
[04:15] Sofia Alvarez: In Private you can configure append-only S3 with object lock and WORM policies. We also provide event signing options for higher assurance; in Hosted we provide checksums and signed delivery to the customer's Kinesis/S3 export but full append-only is typically achieved on the customer's side.
[04:33] Anita Rao: Data residency — some of our customers are EU-based and we need EU-only processing. Can we pin models and requests to a specific region?
[04:41] Liam Chen: Yes, we support region pinning and regional model variants. For Hosted we host in multiple regions and can route requests to EU nodes. For Dedicated/Private you control the region. We can also provide a data processing addendum for EU data residency.
[04:56] Jordan Wells: On retention of generated outputs — we do not want logs of model outputs to persist beyond 30 days. Is that doable?
[05:03] Sofia Alvarez: Yes, you can set retention windows per-route or per-model. For strict setups we recommend Dedicated/Private where you can set enforcement policies or route outputs to ephemeral stores. Hosted will honor retention settings but for strict deletion guarantees you'll want Dedicated/Private and to also control the underlying storage lifecycle.
[05:20] [05:20] Priya Menon: Another item — do you support field-level encryption or tokenization to avoid sending raw PII to the model?
[05:28] Evan Brooks: We have native SDK helpers for client-side field tokenization and support a middleware pattern where PII can be redacted before sending. Also for very sensitive fields, you can use a proxying pattern with local preprocessing and store mapping keys in your KMS.
[05:42] Anita Rao: What about SOC2 and ISO — do you have attestations and can we get them?
[05:48] Liam Chen: Yes, Redwood maintains SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 certificates. I'll send the redacted reports and a one-page control mapping.
[05:57] Marco Lin: On network-level encryption, are connections TLS 1.3 and do you support mTLS for service-to-service?
[06:03] Sofia Alvarez: Yes, TLS 1.3 is used everywhere. mTLS between internal services in Private is supported and we can enable client cert auth for connectors in Dedicated setups where PrivateLink is used.
[06:15] [06:15] Jordan Wells: Performance question — if we run a dedicated GPU pool with quantized models, do we still get the same audit fidelity? I don't want logs to be sampled differently for performance reasons.
[06:25] Evan Brooks: You get full fidelity logs regardless of quantization — sampling is an opt-in optimization to save cost and we won't sample audit logs by default for Dedicated. You can enable or disable sampling per-route.
[06:38] Priya Menon: Is there an SSO provisioning flow for service principals and machine users? We want bots to have long-lived tokens but be revocable.
[06:47] Sofia Alvarez: Yes, we support service accounts with scoped API keys and short-lived JWTs issued by your IdP. Keys are rotatable and can be revoked via the admin API. We recommend short-lived tokens combined with a refresh mechanism for bots.
[06:59] Anita Rao: For the pilot, we want to validate KMS wrap/unwrap and SAML login plus audit export to our Splunk instance. Can Redwood produce a small test harness?
[07:07] Liam Chen: Absolutely — Sofia will outline the pilot runbook. We'll need your SAML metadata and a test Splunk endpoint to push logs.
[07:15] Priya Menon: We'll also want a small regression eval to ensure model outputs don't leak sensitive tokens — is there a way to integrate Redwood's optimize/regression checks into the pilot?
[07:24] Evan Brooks: We have a light eval harness that can run prompt sets and do diff checks; we can include that as part of the pilot and evaluate for leakage heuristics.
[07:33] [07:33] Marco Lin: One operational ask — how do software updates happen on Dedicated? Will you do rolling upgrades or do we control patch window?
[07:41] Sofia Alvarez: We do rolling upgrades by default and provide maintenance windows. For Dedicated you can opt into automatic updates or schedule a maintenance window; for Private you control upgrade orchestration.
[07:53] Jordan Wells: SLA questions — do you have a guaranteed latency SLO for Hosted vs Dedicated?
[07:58] Liam Chen: We publish performance profiles for models and can include latency SLOs in the Dedicated contract. Hosted has best-effort tiers; Dedicated gets tighter commitments. Private SLAs are negotiated.
[08:09] Anita Rao: Compliance reviewers will ask about data deletion proof. Can you provide artifact logs showing deletion occurred?
[08:16] Evan Brooks: Yes, our deletion flows emit audit events with object ids and deletion timestamps which can be exported. For Private you can enforce customer-side immutability and provide verifiable deletion evidence.
[08:29] [08:29] Priya Menon: Are there any known security limitations or things to watch out for? Like, is there any part of the stack that still stores temporary unencrypted payloads on disk?
[08:39] Sofia Alvarez: We avoid storing unencrypted payloads on disk; ephemeral caches and KV caches are encrypted in memory and keys are not persisted in plaintext. However, you should be aware that third-party integrations (if enabled) may have their own retention characteristics, which we'll document. We'll also provide a control mapping and risk register for the pilot.
[08:58] Marco Lin: Ok, timeline — we want to move quickly. Can we do a dedicated pilot for 2-3 weeks starting early July?
[09:05] Liam Chen: That should be doable. We'll send a runbook and pricing estimate this week.
[09:09] Evan Brooks: We'll also include a short test plan: KMS wrap/unwrap, SAML SSO login, SCIM provisioning test, audit export to Splunk, and a regression eval run.
[09:20] Anita Rao: Great. One final question — do you have an incident response playbook and can we map contacts?
[09:27] Sofia Alvarez: Yes, we have an IR playbook and a SOC contact rotation. We'll share the on-call procedures and contact list. For Dedicated customers we provide a technical account manager.
[09:36] Jordan Wells: Ok that's helpful.
[09:38] [09:38] Liam Chen: Quick recap: Redwood to share SOC2/ISO docs, SEs to share pilot runbook and test plan, customer to share SAML metadata and Splunk endpoint, Marco to propose times for pilot planning call. We'll aim to get the pilot started in early July.
[09:55] Priya Menon: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[10:00] Liam Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs and calendar invite.
---
Post-call notes: small transcription artifacts — numbers and acronyms occasionally mis-transcribed (e.g., 'sock two' for SOC2). Action items captured above.
notes: Customer leans toward Dedicated but wants Private-like guarantees for KMS and retention. Agreed pilot to validate SAML+KMS+audit export to Splunk. Redwood to provide SOC2/ISO artifacts and pilot runbook. Pilot target: early July.
